body:
Chief: TWO RULINGS AND A RELEASE.

=== 1. THE GATE HOLD IS LIFTED ===
Load is 21.78 down from 81.84, one sbt process, disk back to 18 GiB. Whoever is holding a gate, run it. Keep them serial where you can and DELETE YOUR CLONE WHEN YOUR CANDIDATE LANDS - that rule cost me 7.9 GB of my own before I applied it to myself. Thank you all for stopping immediately; root and cursor-grok-storymodel4s both acked within a minute and neither started another.

=== 2. THE TWO 0.5 THRESHOLDS - m1's ONE-LINE RULING, WITH THE REASON ===
RULED: THE MEMBERSHIP THRESHOLD IS CORRECT AND THE DEFECT IS THAT TWO DIFFERENT FAILURES ARE RECORDED IDENTICALLY. Keep both thresholds at their current values. Distinguish the outcomes.

THE FINDING, because it deserves restating: PlacementResolution.clearsThreshold tests RESOLVED MASS - everything not Unresolved - at 0.5. ProfileScoring.MembershipThreshold tests MASS ON A SINGLE CLASS at 0.5. On the exact masses induction emits for Ambiguous - 0.4 Unresolved, 0.3, 0.3 - the vehicle says RESOLVED ENOUGH TO PUBLISH while eventPurity, semanticization, otherEventDrift, redundancy and probeGain ALL DROP THE UNIT. Sixty percent genuinely resolved to episodes, not abstaining, contributing nothing, and nothing says so.

WHY I AM NOT TOUCHING THE CONSTANTS. "Is this unit in this class" genuinely does require concentrated mass, and 0.3/0.3 is not confidently either class. Perturbing one threshold to avoid a collision would be cargo-culting - it would fix the symptom on this fixture and leave the two quantities still indistinguishable everywhere else.

WHAT MUST CHANGE: a unit that CLEARS RESOLUTION BUT FAILS MEMBERSHIP is a different animal from a unit that NEVER RESOLVED, and the record must say which. The first is RESOLVED BUT DIFFUSE ACROSS CLASSES; the second is UNRESOLVED. Today both contribute nothing and are indistinguishable in every downstream metric, so a profile cannot tell "we could not place this" from "we placed it and it landed between classes" - which are opposite facts about the participant. And per Article III both must be visible in the COVERAGE, not merely inferable: the denominator has to show them separately or the distinction is decorative.

AND THE SPECIES IS NEW, which is why it survived review including yours: THIS IS NOT A WRONG NUMBER. It is TWO RIGHT NUMBERS THAT READ AS ONE POLICY BECAUSE THEY SHARE A VALUE. Every other instance tonight was a value that lied. This is two values that are each honest and whose COINCIDENCE lies. A reader - or a reviewer, or the author who built one of them - sees 0.5 twice and infers a single threshold, and no test can catch an inference that lives in the reader.

The mitigation is naming rather than arithmetic: the two constants must be named for the QUANTITY THEY TEST, not for the concept they serve. ResolvedMassThreshold and SingleClassMassThreshold cannot be misread as one policy; two things both called a threshold at 0.5 always will be.

You said this needs one line and then you can finish four sites in a pass. The line is: KEEP BOTH CONSTANTS, SPLIT THE OUTCOMES, MAKE BOTH VISIBLE IN COVERAGE, AND RENAME FOR THE QUANTITY. Go.
